info.bio:
Meat Loaf (pedazo de carne) (* 27 de septiembre de 1947) es el nombre artístico de Marvin Lee Aday (cambiado en 2001), es un actor y cantante de rock estadounidense. También bajo el nombre de Meat Loaf se conoce a la banda que lidera y de la que es vocalista. Es conocido por su álbum Bat out of Hell y por muchas canciones pertenecientes a bandas sonoras de películas.

Comienza su carrera musical con 20 años, en Los Ángeles, con la banda "Meat Loaf Soul", siendo teloneros de The Who, The Stooges y Ted Nugent.

scenes.name: Techno-rock y pop de estudio
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El «sonido» por encima de la melodía, el ritmo y la armonía: Electric Light Orchestra inventa el «high-tech pop»; Supertramp, Alan Parsons Project, Kansas, Styx y Split Enz. El valor de la producción define a Steely Dan (el pop-jazz pulido de los yuppies), Hall & Oates, los Fleetwood Mac de Rumours y Tusk, Toto, el «muro de sonido» titánico de Jim Steinman (Bat Out Of Hell) y la Penguin Cafe Orchestra. A finales de los setenta, el art-rock culmina en los supergrupos: 10cc, Godley & Creme, Foreigner, UK, Asia, Sky.

scenes.name: College-pop y nacimiento del lo-fi
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La población universitaria del Sur adopta la ética de la new wave y la adapta a la melodía: un pop inusualmente intelectual, con raíces en el folk-rock y el country-rock pero contaminado por las neurosis de la época. Athens (Georgia) compite con las capitales del rock: B-52's y R.E.M., uno de los grupos de más éxito de la historia. Carolina del Norte (dB's, Windbreakers), Hoboken (Smithereens, Bongos, Tiny Lights), el nacimiento del lo-fi (Half Japanese, Violent Femmes, Beat Happening, Guided By Voices, Sebadoh), They Might Be Giants, Green, B.A.L.L., Boston (Volcano Suns, 10,000 Maniacs, Throwing Muses, Blake Babies), la Costa Oeste (Game Theory, Posies, Young Fresh Fellows) y la sátira de Ween.

podcast.title: Inspired by Ben Dorsi in "Roadie" (1980)
podcast.body: Meat Loaf starred in the 1980 movie "Roadie," where his role was inspired by the life and experiences of Ben Dorsi, often regarded as the first modern roadie. "There was a 1980 movie called Roadie starring Meatloaf in a role inspired by Dorsi."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

podcast.title: Acting Background
podcast.body: Meat Loaf was an actor, serving as an understudy to John Belushi on the National Lampoon Roadshow. His love for acting was evident in his musical performances, particularly in "Paradise by the Dashboard Light," which bassist Kasim Sulton noted was "indelibly linked to his whole life." "And Meatloaf was an actor. He was the understudy to John Belushi on the National Lampoon Roadshow, and he met Steinman in the early 70s when he auditioned for Steinman's 1973 musical More Than You Deserve."

podcast.title: COVID-19 as Cause of Death
podcast.body: Meat Loaf died on January 20th at age 74, and despite a history of various health problems, it was ultimately COVID-19 that claimed his life. "He'd had many health problems over the years, but it appears that it was COVID that finally did him in at age 74."

podcast.title: Declined to Perform for Donald Trump
podcast.body: Meat Loaf turned down various requests to perform for Donald Trump, joining a list of artists who chose not to show musical support. "The killers, Celine Dion, Meat Lough and Erasmith all turned him down to play various things."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Guantanamo Bay Torture
podcast.body: Meat Loaf's music was among the tracks used for musical torture at Camp Delta, the military prison at Guantanamo Bay. Prisoners were sometimes forced to listen to it, even through headphones, for extended periods during interrogation. "If it wasn't Eminem, the music came from Dr. Dre and Meatloaf, sometimes while being forced to wear headphones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Performance of Paradise by the Dashboard Light
podcast.body: According to bassist Kasim Sulton, Meat Loaf deeply enjoyed performing "Paradise by the Dashboard Light," which allowed him to fully embody an acting role. Sulton observed that Meat Loaf brought this theatricality to every song, but especially to "Paradise," feeling a profound personal connection to the material. "Meat got to act in that song, and he loved acting. He did that with every song, but especially in Paradise because it was indelibly linked to his whole life. He loved performing that song more than I could possibly tell you."

podcast.title: Successful Singer in the 70s and 80s
podcast.body: Meat Loaf was one of the most successful singers of the 1970s and 1980s. "Meatloaf, one of the most successful singers of the 70s and 80s."

xref.title: Collaboration with Jim Steinman
xref.body: In the late 1980s, the band collaborated with songwriter Jim Steinman, known for his work with Meat Loaf and Bonnie Tyler, to infuse their doom and gloom with an interesting rock dynamic. "That was most evident in the late 1980s when they teamed up with songwriter Jim Steinman, the guy behind Meatloaf's Battle of Hell."

xref.title: Inspiration for "Roadie" Movie and "King of the Roadies" Documentary
xref.body: In 1980, a movie titled "Roadie" starring Meat Loaf was released, with the lead role explicitly inspired by Ben Dorsi's life and career. Dorsi was also the subject of his own documentary called "King of the Roadies." "There was a 1980 movie called Roadie starring Meatloaf in a role inspired by Dorsi. And Dorsi was the subject of a documentary called King of the Rodies."
